reason: A genuine capital and identity inflection, and still not a Formula E signal. CoVolt Power, Inc. filed a Form S-1 with the SEC on 21 August 2026 for a proposed NYSE listing under the ticker KVLT, an offering estimated at about $200 million. The company itself is new only as a name: it is the rebrand of Signal Energy and Applied High Voltage into one platform, founded in 2005, headquartered in Houston with more than 1,000 staff, and it is a real business - $596 million of revenue for the twelve months to 30 June 2026, $308 million in the first half on $35.4 million of net income, 7.3 GWac of generation built, nearly 1.7 GWh of battery storage and transmission and distribution work connecting more than 26 GW to the grid. Deal-capable, in-window, and profitable, so the screen is not about money. It is about whether Formula E does anything for it. CoVolt is an engineering, procurement and construction contractor selling to US independent power producers, developers, utilities, industrials and data-centre operators; those buyers are won on bonding capacity, safety record, schedule and price, and there are perhaps a few hundred of them. It sells nothing outside the United States, has no product an FE team could use, and no consumer or recruitment brand problem that a livery solves. Formula E's US presence for Season 13 is two rounds - the new Austin E-Prix at the Circuit of The Americas and Miami - so even the Texas hook amounts to one weekend of hospitality a year for a company whose customers are already reachable by name. Honest scoring puts ops fit at 9-10 and brand fit at 10: about 60/100 overall, well under threshold, and inflating it to reach 70 would be exactly the 'plausible company plus a logo' the standard forbids. A further practical point: a company in SEC registration is in a quiet period and cannot announce a sponsorship until the offering prices, so even a good case here would be a 2027 conversation. Leadership checked: Robert L. Tabb, President and CEO; Ronnie V. Shields, CFO; Samuel K. Robison, Chief Legal Officer; no chief marketing officer is listed and no motorsport tie was found.
